official_title: Shall the City Charter of the City of Houston be amended to 1) require the Houston Police Department to make enforcement of Class A and Class B misdemeanor marijuana possession its lowest law-enforcement priority with related reporting requirements and 2) prohibit Houston police officers from requesting or executing "no-knock" search warrants?
plain_summary: Adds a "Houston Freedom Act" to the city charter. Houston police would have to treat misdemeanor marijuana possession as their lowest enforcement priority, the city would audit five years of marijuana arrests and report every year, and officers could no longer request or serve warrants that skip knocking, announcing themselves and waiting 15 seconds. It does not legalize marijuana.
yes_means: A YES vote writes these rules into the charter: misdemeanor marijuana possession becomes HPD's lowest priority, with an audit and yearly public reports, and no-knock warrants are banned.
no_means: A NO vote leaves the charter unchanged; HPD keeps setting its marijuana enforcement and no-knock warrant rules through department policy, which a mayor or police chief can change.
current_law: Marijuana possession is still illegal under Texas law, and up to four ounces is a misdemeanor. After the 2019 Harding Street raid, HPD began requiring the police chief to personally approve any no-knock warrant. Mayor John Whitmire has said no-knock warrants were not served under him or his predecessor. Harris County has offered a marijuana diversion class since 2017, but a new state law limiting district attorneys' discretion has put that program in question.
fiscal_impact: No official city cost estimate was found. The full text requires a one-time audit (due within 120 days of taking effect) and annual reports, and tells the city to track spending on THC testing. FOX 26 said it could not verify the campaign's cost and savings figures.
confusing_wording_note: One YES or NO covers two different policies: marijuana enforcement and the no-knock warrant ban. You cannot vote on them separately. The ballot words never say "Houston Freedom Act" or "decriminalize." "Lowest priority" does not make marijuana legal, and officers keep their discretion to arrest or cite. The audit, yearly reports, diversion policy and THC-testing budget rules are in the full charter text but not in the ballot words. Some news coverage says the measure stops police from using marijuana odor as a reason to search; the official text posted by the city contains no odor rule. The text says it applies "unless and until" a court rules otherwise, and any part a court strikes down is cut while the rest stays.

supporters_case.text: Ground Game Texas, the group behind the petition, says writing the rules into the charter keeps them in place when city leaders change, reduces unequal enforcement, and keeps a low-level arrest from costing people jobs and homes. It says the no-knock ban, inspired by the 2019 Harding Street raid, protects both residents and officers.

opponents_case.text: No organized "vote no" campaign was found. South Texas College of Law Houston professor Tom Hogan opposes a blanket ban, saying no-knock warrants should stay available for rare, high-risk cases with a judge as the check. He also notes a lower priority does not stop officers from enforcing the law.

jurisdiction: Cypress-Fairbanks ISD (northwest Harris County, including part of northwest Houston)
official_title: THIS IS A TAX INCREASE Ratifying the ad valorem tax rate of $1.1569 in Cypress-Fairbanks Independent School District for the current year, a rate that will result in an increase of 23 percent in maintenance and operations tax revenue for the district for the current year as compared to the preceding year, which is an additional $102,350,532.
plain_summary: Asks Cy-Fair ISD voters to approve the $1.1569 per $100 tax rate the board adopted for this year. The district says it raises day-to-day operating money (salaries, utilities, programs) by 23%, about $102.4 million more than last year.
yes_means: A YES vote approves the $1.1569 rate and the extra $102.4 million for operations.
no_means: A NO vote rolls the rate back to the voter-approval rate; the district does not get the extra $102.4 million.
fiscal_impact: An additional $102,350,532 in maintenance and operations revenue, per the ballot language. Your own bill depends on your appraised value and exemptions.
confusing_wording_note: A VATRE (voter-approval tax rate election) asks voters to ratify a school tax rate above the state cap. The 23% figure is the growth in operating revenue, not your tax bill. This is separate from the four bond questions (B to E), which pay for buildings and equipment.

jurisdiction: Cypress-Fairbanks ISD (northwest Harris County, including part of northwest Houston)
official_title: THIS IS A PROPERTY TAX INCREASE. The issuance of $1,299,520,000 of bonds for the improvement, capital renovation, repair and replacement, and equipment of and additions to existing school buildings in the District, for the purchase of new school buses, for the retrofitting of school buses with emergency, safety, or security equipment, and for the purchase or retrofitting of vehicles to be used for emergency, safety, or security purposes, and the levying of a tax sufficient to pay the principal of and interest on the bonds and to pay the costs of any credit agreements executed or authorized in anticipation of, in relation to or in connection with the bonds.
plain_summary: Lets Cy-Fair ISD borrow up to $1.3 billion to repair, renovate and add on to existing schools, buy new buses, and add safety equipment to buses and security vehicles.
yes_means: A YES vote lets the district sell up to $1,299,520,000 in bonds for these projects and repay them with property taxes.
no_means: A NO vote means the district cannot sell these bonds.
current_law: Cy-Fair ISD owes $3,264,440,000 in principal on existing debt (about $4.6 billion with interest) and levies a $0.40 per $100 debt tax.
fiscal_impact: District estimate: $2,837,363,167 in principal and interest over the life of the bonds, issued in five yearly batches from 2026 to 2030. The district projects $0 added tax on a $100,000 homestead (after the state's $140,000 homestead exemption) and says B through E together could be paid while lowering its debt tax rate from $0.40 to $0.37.
confusing_wording_note: Texas law makes every bond ballot say "THIS IS A PROPERTY TAX INCREASE," even when, as here, the district projects its debt tax rate will go down. Vote FOR to approve the borrowing, AGAINST to reject it.

jurisdiction: Spring ISD (north Harris County, including part of north Houston)
official_title: THIS IS A TAX INCREASE Ratifying the ad valorem tax rate of $1.1569 in Spring Independent School District for the current year, a rate that will result in an increase of 0 percent in maintenance and operations tax revenue for the district for the current year as compared to the preceding year, which is an additional $0.
plain_summary: Asks Spring ISD voters to approve the $1.1569 per $100 tax rate the board adopted for this year. The required ballot wording says it raises operating revenue by 0%, an additional $0.
yes_means: A YES vote approves the $1.1569 rate the board adopted.
no_means: A NO vote rolls the rate back to the voter-approval rate.
fiscal_impact: The ballot language states a 0 percent increase and an additional $0 in maintenance and operations revenue. We found no district explanation of why an election is needed at 0%.
confusing_wording_note: The ballot opens with "THIS IS A TAX INCREASE" and then says the increase is 0 percent and $0. Both phrases are required wording. The rate shown matches Cy-Fair ISD's to the hundredth of a cent, so check the wording on your own ballot at harrisvotes.com.

jurisdiction: Huffman ISD (northeast Harris County, touching Houston's Lake Houston area)
official_title: THIS IS A TAX INCREASE Ratifying the ad valorem tax rate of $1.0637 in Huffman Independent School District for the current year, a rate that will result in an increase of 4.88 percent in maintenance and operations tax revenue for the district for the current year as compared to the preceding year, which is an additional $ -20.30.
plain_summary: Asks Huffman ISD voters to approve the $1.0637 per $100 tax rate the board adopted, which the ballot says raises operating revenue 4.88%.
yes_means: A YES vote approves the $1.0637 rate.
no_means: A NO vote rolls the rate back to the voter-approval rate.
fiscal_impact: The ballot states a 4.88 percent increase but lists the added dollars as "$ -20.30," which does not match. We found no district explanation.
confusing_wording_note: The official wording contains an apparent error: a 4.88% increase described as an additional negative $20.30. The rest of the question works like any VATRE: FOR keeps the adopted rate, AGAINST rolls it back.
